# _autosummary/ir.index.html.md

# ir.index

The indexing pipeline and incremental maintenance.

[`build()`](_autosummary/ir.index.html.md#ir.index.build) turns a [`CorpusSource`](_autosummary/ir.sources.html.md#ir.sources.CorpusSource) into a queryable
[`Corpus`](_autosummary/ir.index.html.md#ir.index.Corpus), persisting records through a
[`CorpusStore`](_autosummary/ir.store.html.md#ir.store.CorpusStore). It is **incremental and idempotent**: each
artifact’s change signal is compared to the ledger, and only new, changed, or
re-modeled artifacts are decomposed and embedded. Artifacts that vanished from
the source are pruned (full-refresh). Re-running `build` on an unchanged
source is a near-no-op.

This is the light maintenance path — content-hash CRUD over a flat store, which
is the right tool for the small corpora `ir` targets. The heavier
content-addressed artifact-graph (`ef.artifact_graph`) is the documented
upgrade for corpora large enough that recomputing surfaces is the bottleneck.

### Functions

| [`build`](_autosummary/ir.index.html.md#ir.index.build)(source, \*[, store, embedder, full, ...])   | Build or incrementally update *source* into a [`Corpus`](_autosummary/ir.index.html.md#ir.index.Corpus).   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`open_corpus`](_autosummary/ir.index.html.md#ir.index.open_corpus)(name, \*[, embedder])                 | Reopen a previously built corpus by name.                                                                |

### Classes

| [`Corpus`](_autosummary/ir.index.html.md#ir.index.Corpus)(name, store, embedder, embedder_id)   | A built, queryable corpus: a store plus its embedder.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* ir.index.Corpus(name, store, embedder, embedder_id)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A built, queryable corpus: a store plus its embedder.

#### search(query, \*\*kwargs)

Search this corpus for *query*.

`**kwargs` (`k` / `mode` / `filter` / `surfaces` /
`per_artifact` / …) are forwarded to [`ir.retrieve.search()`](_autosummary/ir.retrieve.html.md#ir.retrieve.search).

### ir.index.build(source, , store=None, embedder=None, full=True, batch_size=256, edge_extractor=None)

Build or incrementally update *source* into a [`Corpus`](_autosummary/ir.index.html.md#ir.index.Corpus).

* **Parameters:**
  * **store** ([`CorpusStore`](_autosummary/ir.store.html.md#ir.store.CorpusStore) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None))
  * **embedder** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any))
  * **full** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool))
  * **batch_size** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int))
  * **edge_extractor** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)]) – (`(artifact_id, filter_fields) -> {edge_type: [target]}`) that
    populates the corpus’s semantic `links` graph (see [`ir.graph`](_autosummary/ir.graph.html.md#module-ir.graph);
    pass [`ir.default_edge_extractor()`](_autosummary/ir.html.md#ir.default_edge_extractor) for the latent deps/parent
    edges). Ingest is **eager** — edges are (re)written for *every*
    in-scope artifact, a decompose-only pass with no embedding, so the
    graph never goes partially stale — while embedding stays fully
    incremental. Edges are derived state, **not** part of build identity.
    A rebuild *without* an extractor leaves existing edges untouched
    (they are only refreshed by re-running with one, and only cleared per
    artifact by the `full` prune below) — so dropping `edge_extractor`
    does not wipe a graph.
* **Return type:**
  [`Corpus`](_autosummary/ir.index.html.md#ir.index.Corpus)

### ir.index.open_corpus(name, , embedder=None)

Reopen a previously built corpus by name.

The embedding model is **lazily** resolved (see `_LazyEmbedder`): the
returned corpus knows its `embedder_id` from stored config immediately, but
only loads the model when a dense/hybrid query actually embeds. So `ir ls`,
`ir info`, and lexical-only search open a corpus without the model-load
cost. Pass `embedder=` to override the stored spec.

Without an override the corpus is \*\*pinned to the embedder it was built
with\*\* (its stored `embedder_id`), not re-resolved from the spec: a spec
like `"default"` means different models on machines with and without
`sentence-transformers`, which would make the query vectors incompatible
with the index.

* **Return type:**
  [`Corpus`](_autosummary/ir.index.html.md#ir.index.Corpus)


# _autosummary/ir.maintenance.html.md

# ir.maintenance

Idempotent background-work runner — `ir maintain` (issue #58).

The *executing* half of ir’s maintenance story (the declarative half is
[`ir.policy`](_autosummary/ir.policy.html.md#module-ir.policy)). [`maintain()`](_autosummary/ir.maintenance.html.md#ir.maintenance.maintain) reads each corpus’s resolved
[`MaintenancePolicy`](_autosummary/ir.policy.html.md#ir.policy.MaintenancePolicy) and does the work that is **due**:

- an **incremental rebuild** when reindex is due (`source-change` is always
  due — the build is a near-no-op when nothing changed; `interval` only when
  stale; `manual` never);
- when `synopsis.enabled`, the rebuild’s strategy is wrapped in
  [`ir.with_synopsis()`](_autosummary/ir.html.md#ir.with_synopsis), so new / changed artifacts gain an LLM synopsis —
  > and because that build may call an LLM, it is run \*\*only inside the policy’s
  > downtime window\*\*.

It is safe to call as often as a scheduler likes: it no-ops when nothing is due,
and records `last_maintained` so interval policies converge. ir runs the work;
*scheduling* it is external — a cron / launchd entry calls `ir maintain --all`
every N minutes, and the downtime window lives in the policy (data), not in ir.

[`ir.schedule`](_autosummary/ir.schedule.html.md#module-ir.schedule) installs that entry for you (`ir schedule`) and reports on it;
it writes a definition and exits, so the executor is still cron / launchd:

```default
# what `ir schedule --every 15m` writes on a cron machine:
*/15 * * * *  <python> -m ir maintain --all >> ~/.cache/ir/maintain.log 2>&1
```

Because a scheduled run has nobody watching it, [`maintain()`](_autosummary/ir.maintenance.html.md#ir.maintenance.maintain) is fault-isolated
per corpus: one corpus failing is recorded on its own result and the sweep carries
on, rather than aborting and leaving the corpora after it silently unmaintained.

### Module Attributes

| [`DFLT_STALE_LOCK_AFTER`](_autosummary/ir.maintenance.html.md#ir.maintenance.DFLT_STALE_LOCK_AFTER)   | A lock older than this is assumed to belong to a run that was killed rather than one still working.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`lock_path`](_autosummary/ir.maintenance.html.md#ir.maintenance.lock_path)()                                     | Where the single-run lock lives (regenerable, so the cache dir).                                      |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`maintain`](_autosummary/ir.maintenance.html.md#ir.maintenance.maintain)([name, all, now, dry_run])             | Run due background work for one corpus (*name*) or every registered one (*all*).                      |
| [`maintain_corpus`](_autosummary/ir.maintenance.html.md#ir.maintenance.maintain_corpus)(name, \*[, now, dry_run, full]) | Do the due background work for one corpus (idempotent).                                               |
| [`single_run`](_autosummary/ir.maintenance.html.md#ir.maintenance.single_run)(\*[, path, stale_after])             | Hold the maintenance lock, or raise [`MaintenanceBusy`](_autosummary/ir.maintenance.html.md#ir.maintenance.MaintenanceBusy). |

### Classes

| [`MaintenanceResult`](_autosummary/ir.maintenance.html.md#ir.maintenance.MaintenanceResult)(name, ran, reason[, ...])   | What [`maintain_corpus()`](_autosummary/ir.maintenance.html.md#ir.maintenance.maintain_corpus) did (or would do) for one corpus.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Exceptions

| [`MaintenanceBusy`](_autosummary/ir.maintenance.html.md#ir.maintenance.MaintenanceBusy)   | Another maintenance run holds the lock.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|

### ir.maintenance.DFLT_STALE_LOCK_AFTER *= datetime.timedelta(seconds=21600)*

A lock older than this is assumed to belong to a run that was killed rather
than one still working. Generous, because a first full build of a large corpus
legitimately takes a long time and reclaiming a *live* lock is the bad outcome.

### *exception* ir.maintenance.MaintenanceBusy

Bases: [`RuntimeError`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError)

Another maintenance run holds the lock.

### *class* ir.maintenance.MaintenanceResult(name, ran, reason, reindex=False, synopsis=False, records=None, error=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

What [`maintain_corpus()`](_autosummary/ir.maintenance.html.md#ir.maintenance.maintain_corpus) did (or would do) for one corpus.

### ir.maintenance.lock_path()

Where the single-run lock lives (regenerable, so the cache dir).

* **Return type:**
  [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)

### ir.maintenance.maintain(name=None, , all=False, now=None, dry_run=False)

Run due background work for one corpus (*name*) or every registered one (*all*).

With neither, defaults to all registered corpora. Returns one
[`MaintenanceResult`](_autosummary/ir.maintenance.html.md#ir.maintenance.MaintenanceResult) per corpus considered.

**A named corpus raises; a sweep records.** Asking for one corpus by name is a
direct request, and swallowing its error would turn a typo’d name into a
result that reads as success to any caller written before `error` existed.
A sweep is the unattended case, where the opposite is true: one corpus
failing must not leave every corpus after it stale with nothing to say so.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`MaintenanceResult`](_autosummary/ir.maintenance.html.md#ir.maintenance.MaintenanceResult)]

### ir.maintenance.maintain_corpus(name, , now=None, dry_run=False, full=True)

Do the due background work for one corpus (idempotent).

Reads the corpus’s resolved policy and its `last_maintained` time, decides
whether a (synopsis-aware) reindex is due *and* permitted now, and — unless
`dry_run` — runs the incremental build and records the run.

* **Return type:**
  [`MaintenanceResult`](_autosummary/ir.maintenance.html.md#ir.maintenance.MaintenanceResult)

### ir.maintenance.single_run(, path=None, stale_after=None)

Hold the maintenance lock, or raise [`MaintenanceBusy`](_autosummary/ir.maintenance.html.md#ir.maintenance.MaintenanceBusy).

Two maintenance runs on one corpus store are not safe: the packed store
rewrites `matrix`/`ids`/`metas` as separate files, so interleaved
writers can leave a matrix whose rows no longer line up with its ids — an
index that answers confidently and wrongly, with nothing raised. launchd
already runs one instance per label, but that does not cover cron (which
happily stacks runs) or the manual `ir maintain --all` this tool’s own
menu suggests while the agent may be mid-run.

A lock whose owning process is gone, or which is older than *stale_after*, is
reclaimed — a killed run must not wedge maintenance forever.


# _autosummary/ir.policy.html.md

# ir.policy

Per-corpus policy — how a corpus is segmented/stored and what background work it gets.

This is the *declarative* half of ir’s maintenance story (issue #58): a corpus’s
policy lives as **data** in its registry entry, and ir resolves an effective
policy by layering `entry` over per-`kind` defaults over a global default.
An idempotent [`ir.maintenance.maintain()`](_autosummary/ir.maintenance.html.md#ir.maintenance.maintain) reads the policy and does the due
work; *scheduling* that work (cron / launchd, or an orchestration layer’s budget
governor) stays **external** — ir never imports an orchestration layer, and there
is no global `Settings` singleton (policy is per-corpus data, injected, not a
process-wide mutable). The light path stays a one-liner: every field has a smart
default, so `ir build skills` needs no policy at all.

The three policy axes:

- **reindex** — *when* to rebuild: `"source-change"` (default; rebuild is a
  near-no-op when nothing changed, so it is always safe to run), `"interval"`
  (only when older than `every_hours`), or `"manual"` (never automatic).
- **synopsis** — *whether/when* to attach LLM synopses (the expensive,
  off-by-default work): only the `recent` slice, only during `downtime_hours`.
  Synopsis is realized as a strategy wrapper ([`ir.with_synopsis()`](_autosummary/ir.html.md#ir.with_synopsis)), so it is
  incremental — only new/changed artifacts are synthesized.
- **storage** — the persistence backend. Today only `"local"` (the file store);
  a `vd.Collection` backend is the documented future seam (issue #28).

### Module Attributes

| [`REINDEX_TRIGGERS`](_autosummary/ir.policy.html.md#ir.policy.REINDEX_TRIGGERS)   | Accepted `reindex.on` triggers.                                   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`STORAGE_BACKENDS`](_autosummary/ir.policy.html.md#ir.policy.STORAGE_BACKENDS)   | Storage backends ir can resolve today.                            |
| [`GLOBAL_DEFAULT`](_autosummary/ir.policy.html.md#ir.policy.GLOBAL_DEFAULT)     | The global fallback policy (any kind without a specific default). |
| [`DEFAULTS_BY_KIND`](_autosummary/ir.policy.html.md#ir.policy.DEFAULTS_BY_KIND)   | Per-kind maintenance defaults.                                    |

### Functions

| [`default_policy_for_kind`](_autosummary/ir.policy.html.md#ir.policy.default_policy_for_kind)(kind)                | The smart-default [`MaintenancePolicy`](_autosummary/ir.policy.html.md#ir.policy.MaintenancePolicy) for a corpus `kind`.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`in_downtime`](_autosummary/ir.policy.html.md#ir.policy.in_downtime)(policy, now)                     | Whether `now` falls inside the synopsis `downtime_hours` window.                                            |
| [`is_reindex_due`](_autosummary/ir.policy.html.md#ir.policy.is_reindex_due)(policy, last_maintained, now) | Whether a reindex is due under `policy` given the last-maintained time.                                     |
| [`resolve_policy`](_autosummary/ir.policy.html.md#ir.policy.resolve_policy)(entry)                        | The effective policy for a registry `entry`: entry over kind over global.                                   |
| [`resolve_storage`](_autosummary/ir.policy.html.md#ir.policy.resolve_storage)(entry)                       | The effective storage spec for an `entry` (default `{"backend": "local"}`).                                 |

### Classes

| [`MaintenancePolicy`](_autosummary/ir.policy.html.md#ir.policy.MaintenancePolicy)([reindex, synopsis])   | The background-work policy for one corpus (reindex + synopsis).   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`ReindexPolicy`](_autosummary/ir.policy.html.md#ir.policy.ReindexPolicy)([on, every_hours])         | When to (incrementally) rebuild a corpus.                         |
| [`SynopsisPolicy`](_autosummary/ir.policy.html.md#ir.policy.SynopsisPolicy)([enabled, scope, ...])    | Whether/when to attach (expensive, LLM-generated) synopses.       |

### ir.policy.DEFAULTS_BY_KIND *: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]* *= {'files': {'reindex': {'on': 'source-change'}}, 'packages': {'reindex': {'on': 'source-change'}}, 'records': {'reindex': {'every_hours': 24, 'on': 'interval'}}, 'reports': {'reindex': {'on': 'source-change'}}, 'sessions': {'reindex': {'every_hours': 24, 'on': 'interval'}, 'synopsis': {'downtime_hours': [2, 6], 'enabled': False, 'scope': 'recent', 'window_days': 30}}, 'skills': {'reindex': {'on': 'source-change'}}}*

Per-kind maintenance defaults. The rule of thumb encoded here:
*small, fully-enumerable* corpora (skills/packages/reports/files) rebuild on
source change (cheap, exact); *large, append-mostly, time-stamped* corpora
(sessions) rebuild on an interval and keep synopsis off by default, with a
downtime window ready for when it is turned on. New kinds register here.

### ir.policy.GLOBAL_DEFAULT *= MaintenancePolicy(reindex=ReindexPolicy(on='source-change', every_hours=None), synopsis=SynopsisPolicy(enabled=False, scope='recent', window_days=30, downtime_hours=None))*

The global fallback policy (any kind without a specific default).

### *class* ir.policy.MaintenancePolicy(reindex=ReindexPolicy(), synopsis=SynopsisPolicy())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The background-work policy for one corpus (reindex + synopsis).

#### merged(override)

Layer an `override` dict on top of this policy (entry over defaults).

* **Return type:**
  [`MaintenancePolicy`](_autosummary/ir.policy.html.md#ir.policy.MaintenancePolicy)

### ir.policy.REINDEX_TRIGGERS *= ('source-change', 'interval', 'manual')*

Accepted `reindex.on` triggers.

### *class* ir.policy.ReindexPolicy(on='source-change', every_hours=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

When to (incrementally) rebuild a corpus.

### ir.policy.STORAGE_BACKENDS *= ('local',)*

Storage backends ir can resolve today. `"vd"` (vd.Collection) is the
documented future backend, gated on issue #28.

### *class* ir.policy.SynopsisPolicy(enabled=False, scope='recent', window_days=30, downtime_hours=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Whether/when to attach (expensive, LLM-generated) synopses.

`downtime_hours` is a `[start, end)` pair of local-clock hours
(wrapping past midnight is allowed, e.g. `(22, 6)`); `None` means
“any time”. `scope="recent"` limits synthesis to artifacts whose
timestamp is within `window_days` (corpora that expose a time signal);
`scope="all"` synthesizes every artifact (bounded by incrementality).

### ir.policy.default_policy_for_kind(kind)

The smart-default [`MaintenancePolicy`](_autosummary/ir.policy.html.md#ir.policy.MaintenancePolicy) for a corpus `kind`.

* **Return type:**
  [`MaintenancePolicy`](_autosummary/ir.policy.html.md#ir.policy.MaintenancePolicy)

### ir.policy.in_downtime(policy, now)

Whether `now` falls inside the synopsis `downtime_hours` window.

`None` window means “any time”. A window whose start hour is greater than
its end hour wraps past midnight (e.g. `(22, 6)` is 22:00–06:00).

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### ir.policy.is_reindex_due(policy, last_maintained, now)

Whether a reindex is due under `policy` given the last-maintained time.

- `source-change` is always due (the build is incremental and a no-op when
  nothing changed, so running it cannot do harm).
- `interval` is due when never maintained or older than `every_hours`.
- `manual` is never automatically due.

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### ir.policy.resolve_policy(entry)

The effective policy for a registry `entry`: entry over kind over global.

A v1 entry (no `maintenance` key) resolves to its kind’s smart default, so
existing corpora gain a sensible policy without a migration.

* **Return type:**
  [`MaintenancePolicy`](_autosummary/ir.policy.html.md#ir.policy.MaintenancePolicy)

### ir.policy.resolve_storage(entry)

The effective storage spec for an `entry` (default `{"backend": "local"}`).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)


# _autosummary/ir.registry.html.md

# ir.registry

Named-corpus registry — persistent, reusable corpus definitions.

A registry entry records *how* to (re)build a corpus — its `kind` (a source
preset), parameters, and embedder spec — so a corpus becomes a stable name you
can build once and query across sessions. The registry is a single JSON file
under the config dir (`~/.config/ir/corpora.json`).

Presets map to [`CorpusSource`](_autosummary/ir.sources.html.md#ir.sources.CorpusSource) constructors:

- `skills`   → `CorpusSource.from_skills()`
- `packages` → `CorpusSource.from_packages()`
- `reports`  → `CorpusSource.from_md_reports()`
- `sessions` → `CorpusSource.from_claude_sessions()`
- `files`    → `CorpusSource.from_files()` (needs `root`; optional
  `pattern`)
- `records`  → `CorpusSource.from_records()` (needs `fetcher`, a
  `"module:attr"` reference; optional `metadata_keys` / `id_key` /
  `text_key`) — the seam for a corpus whose records another package owns

Unregistered preset names (`skills`/`packages`/`reports`/`sessions`) are
auto-registered with defaults on first use, so `ir build skills` just works.

### Module Attributes

| [`PARAMETRIC_KINDS`](_autosummary/ir.registry.html.md#ir.registry.PARAMETRIC_KINDS)   | Kinds that need parameters, so they are never auto-registered from a bare name.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`get`](_autosummary/ir.registry.html.md#ir.registry.get)(name)                                 | The registry entry for *name*, or `None`.                                                                                                 |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`policy_for`](_autosummary/ir.registry.html.md#ir.registry.policy_for)(name)                          | The effective [`ir.policy.MaintenancePolicy`](_autosummary/ir.policy.html.md#ir.policy.MaintenancePolicy) for corpus *name*. |
| [`register`](_autosummary/ir.registry.html.md#ir.registry.register)(name, kind, \*[, embedder, ...]) | Register (or overwrite) a named corpus definition.                                                                                        |
| [`registered`](_autosummary/ir.registry.html.md#ir.registry.registered)()                              | All registered corpus definitions, keyed by name.                                                                                         |
| [`retriever_for`](_autosummary/ir.registry.html.md#ir.registry.retriever_for)(name, \*\*search_defaults)  | A [`Retriever`](_autosummary/ir.retrieve.html.md#ir.retrieve.Retriever) bound to the registered corpus *name*.                 |
| [`retrievers`](_autosummary/ir.registry.html.md#ir.registry.retrievers)(\*\*search_defaults)           | A lazy `Mapping[name, Retriever]` view over the registry (ir_09 §8).                                                                      |
| [`source_for`](_autosummary/ir.registry.html.md#ir.registry.source_for)(name)                          | Resolve *name* to a source, auto-registering a preset if needed.                                                                          |
| [`source_from_entry`](_autosummary/ir.registry.html.md#ir.registry.source_from_entry)(name, entry)            | Reconstruct a `CorpusSource` from a registry entry.                                                                                       |
| [`unregister`](_autosummary/ir.registry.html.md#ir.registry.unregister)(name)                          | Remove *name* from the registry (does not delete built data).                                                                             |

### ir.registry.PARAMETRIC_KINDS *= ('files', 'records')*

Kinds that need parameters, so they are never auto-registered from a bare name.

### ir.registry.get(name)

The registry entry for *name*, or `None`.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### ir.registry.policy_for(name)

The effective [`ir.policy.MaintenancePolicy`](_autosummary/ir.policy.html.md#ir.policy.MaintenancePolicy) for corpus *name*.

Resolves the registered entry’s `maintenance` over its kind’s smart default
over the global default (see [`ir.policy.resolve_policy()`](_autosummary/ir.policy.html.md#ir.policy.resolve_policy)). An unregistered
name resolves to the global default policy.

### ir.registry.register(name, kind, , embedder='default', strategy=None, maintenance=None, storage=None, \*\*params)

Register (or overwrite) a named corpus definition.

Beyond the v1 `kind` / `embedder` / `params`, an entry may now carry
(all optional, with smart per-kind defaults applied at resolution time — see
[`ir.policy`](_autosummary/ir.policy.html.md#module-ir.policy)):

- `strategy` — an [`IndexingStrategy`](_autosummary/ir.strategy.html.md#ir.strategy.IndexingStrategy) (or a
  `{"name", "params"}` spec) persisted so the corpus’s *segmentation* is
  stable across rebuilds. `None` keeps the preset’s default strategy.
- `maintenance` — the background-work policy dict (`reindex` / `synopsis`;
  validated here, see [`ir.policy.MaintenancePolicy`](_autosummary/ir.policy.html.md#ir.policy.MaintenancePolicy)).
- `storage` — the persistence backend (default `{"backend": "local"}`).

Entries written by older `ir` (none of these keys) keep working unchanged.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### ir.registry.registered()

All registered corpus definitions, keyed by name.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

### ir.registry.retriever_for(name, \*\*search_defaults)

A [`Retriever`](_autosummary/ir.retrieve.html.md#ir.retrieve.Retriever) bound to the registered corpus *name*.

Opens the corpus (it must have been built) and wraps it with
[`ir.as_retriever()`](_autosummary/ir.html.md#ir.as_retriever); `search_defaults` (e.g. `mode="hybrid"`) bind to
every call.

### ir.registry.retrievers(\*\*search_defaults)

A lazy `Mapping[name, Retriever]` view over the registry (ir_09 §8).

The query-time projection of the build-recipe registry: each value is a
ready-to-call [`Retriever`](_autosummary/ir.retrieve.html.md#ir.retrieve.Retriever). This is the source-registry
facade an orchestration layer (`raglab`) consumes — it never opens a corpus
until the key is accessed, and always reflects the current [`registered()`](_autosummary/ir.registry.html.md#ir.registry.registered)
set. `search_defaults` apply to every source.

* **Return type:**
  [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

### ir.registry.source_for(name)

Resolve *name* to a source, auto-registering a preset if needed.

* **Return type:**
  [`CorpusSource`](_autosummary/ir.sources.html.md#ir.sources.CorpusSource)

### ir.registry.source_from_entry(name, entry)

Reconstruct a `CorpusSource` from a registry entry.

A persisted `strategy` spec (registry v2) is reconstructed and passed to
the preset constructor, so a corpus’s segmentation survives across rebuilds.
A v1 entry (no `strategy`) passes `strategy=None` and keeps the preset’s
default — unchanged behavior.

* **Return type:**
  [`CorpusSource`](_autosummary/ir.sources.html.md#ir.sources.CorpusSource)

### ir.registry.unregister(name)

Remove *name* from the registry (does not delete built data).

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)


# _autosummary/ir.requirements.html.md

# ir.requirements

Dependency check for `ir`: name what is missing and how to install it.

`ir` imports its dependencies deep inside `ir/base.py` and friends; on an
interpreter that lacks them (a fresh server’s system `python3`) that surfaces
as a bare `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'numpy'` that says nothing
about `ir` or the fix. [`check_requirements()`](_autosummary/ir.requirements.html.md#ir.requirements.check_requirements) runs first, from
`ir/__init__.py`, using only the standard library, and raises
[`MissingRequirements`](_autosummary/ir.requirements.html.md#ir.requirements.MissingRequirements) (a [`ModuleNotFoundError`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ModuleNotFoundError)) listing every
missing import, the interpreter it was looked up in, and the install commands.
It also checks the version bounds `ir` declares for them (`cw>=0.1.1,<0.2`),
read from `ir`’s installed metadata, and raises [`UnsatisfiedRequirements`](_autosummary/ir.requirements.html.md#ir.requirements.UnsatisfiedRequirements)
for an installed dependency outside them, instead of an opaque error later.

### Module Attributes

| [`DIST`](_autosummary/ir.requirements.html.md#ir.requirements.DIST)     | the distribution whose declared requirements hold the version bounds   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`REQUIRED`](_autosummary/ir.requirements.html.md#ir.requirements.REQUIRED) | import name -> distribution name, for everything `import ir` needs.    |

### Functions

| [`check_requirements`](_autosummary/ir.requirements.html.md#ir.requirements.check_requirements)([required, bounds])       | Raise [`MissingRequirements`](_autosummary/ir.requirements.html.md#ir.requirements.MissingRequirements) unless every dependency is importable, then [`UnsatisfiedRequirements`](_autosummary/ir.requirements.html.md#ir.requirements.UnsatisfiedRequirements) unless each is within the bounds `ir` declares (*bounds*: `{name: specifier}`, default read from `ir`'s metadata).   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`declared_bounds`](_autosummary/ir.requirements.html.md#ir.requirements.declared_bounds)([dist])                      | `{normalized dependency name: specifier}` that *dist*'s installed metadata declares for this environment (extras excluded; the specifiers of repeated names are joined); empty when *dist* is not installed or has none.                                                                                             |
| [`missing_requirements`](_autosummary/ir.requirements.html.md#ir.requirements.missing_requirements)([required])             | Distribution names in *required* whose import name cannot be found.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| [`requirements_message`](_autosummary/ir.requirements.html.md#ir.requirements.requirements_message)(missing)                | The actionable message for *missing* distributions.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| [`unsatisfied_message`](_autosummary/ir.requirements.html.md#ir.requirements.unsatisfied_message)(unsatisfied)             | The actionable message for *unsatisfied* `(dist, installed, specifier)`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| [`unsatisfied_requirements`](_autosummary/ir.requirements.html.md#ir.requirements.unsatisfied_requirements)([required, bounds]) | `(distribution, installed version, specifier)` of each dependency in *required* that is installed outside its declared bounds.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| [`version_satisfies`](_autosummary/ir.requirements.html.md#ir.requirements.version_satisfies)(installed, specifier)      | Whether *installed* meets *specifier* (`'>=0.1.1,<0.2'`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

### Exceptions

| [`MissingRequirements`](_autosummary/ir.requirements.html.md#ir.requirements.MissingRequirements)     | `ir`'s dependencies are missing from the running interpreter.            |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`UnsatisfiedRequirements`](_autosummary/ir.requirements.html.md#ir.requirements.UnsatisfiedRequirements) | A dependency is installed in a version outside the bounds `ir` declares. |

  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

`(distribution, installed version, specifier)` of each dependency in
*required* that is installed outside its declared bounds.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]

### ir.requirements.version_satisfies(installed, specifier)

Whether *installed* meets *specifier* (`'>=0.1.1,<0.2'`).

Uses `packaging` when it is installed. Without it, plain releases (`1.2.3`)
are compared with the standard library, and anything it cannot judge (a
pre-release, `dev`, `post` or local version, an unreadable specifier) is taken
to hold: this check must never block `import ir` on a doubt.

```pycon
>>> version_satisfies("0.1.6", ">=0.1.1,<0.2"), version_satisfies("0.2.0", "<0.2")
(True, False)
>>> version_satisfies("1.4", "~=1.2"), version_satisfies("2.0", "~=1.2")
(True, False)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)


# _autosummary/ir.rerank.html.md

# ir.rerank

The precision stage: a cross-encoder rerank over the first-stage candidates.

First-stage retrieval (dense / lexical / hybrid) is tuned for *recall*; many of its worst
false positives are artefacts a joint `(query, passage)` scorer catches – a package
whose single “DAG” bullet inflates its pooled-vector cosine, or a pair of siblings that
share jargon rather than topic. [`ir.search()`](_autosummary/ir.html.md#ir.search) therefore takes `rerank=`: it
over-fetches `fetch_k` candidates, hands them to the reranker, and keeps the top `k`.
This is single-shot and agent-free: a better *one* search, not the evaluator back-edge
(that belongs to `raglab`).

`ir` composes `ef` here and adds no reranker class. `ef.cross_encoder_reranker` is the
implementation; this module adds the three things `ef` cannot know about an `ir` corpus:

- **What the reranker reads.** `rerank_text="surface"` (default) scores the matched
  surface, exactly as before. `"artifact"` scores the artifact’s *whole* stored text –
  its sibling surfaces (name + description + README chunks) joined in plan order – so a
  thin description is judged against the full README. A callable
  `(corpus, meta) -> str` replaces both.
- **Opt-in, with a graceful fallback.** `rerank="cross-encoder"` (or
  `"cross-encoder:<model>"`) names the ef cross-encoder without importing it, so
  `import ir` needs no torch. When `sentence-transformers` (the `ir[rerank]` extra) is
  missing, the search warns once and returns the first-stage ranking rather than failing.
- **Calibration that stays honest.** A reranked hit’s score is the reranker’s, on a scale
  unrelated to cosine / RRF / BM25, so an abstention floor calibrated for `hybrid` would
  be mis-scaled if applied to it. [`calibration_key()`](_autosummary/ir.rerank.html.md#ir.rerank.calibration_key) gives a reranked configuration its
  own key (`hybrid+rerank-<model>+artifact`), so `calibrate_min_score(...,
  rerank=...)` and `discover(..., min_score="auto", rerank=...)` read and write a floor
  for *that* configuration, and fall back to “no floor” (with the usual warning) rather
  than a wrong one. The fallback to first-stage ranking maps back to the plain key.

Relative selection strategies (`rel_threshold`, `score_gap`…) compare score *ratios*,
so a reranker used with them must return non-negative scores. The `"cross-encoder"` spec
guarantees that: most cross-encoders (including ef’s default ms-marco model) return raw
logits that run negative, so ir passes them through a sigmoid into `(0, 1)`. (A model that already applies a sigmoid would be squashed a second time, which keeps the
order but compresses the scale until relative selectors can no longer tell hits apart: use
such a model as a callable, `ef.cross_encoder_reranker(model)` with a `rerank_id`.) A callable you pass yourself is used as is: keep it in
`[0, 1]`, or give it a stable `rerank_id` attribute so its calibrated floor is kept apart.

```pycon
>>> resolve_reranker(None) is None
True
>>> calibration_key("hybrid", None)
'hybrid'
>>> calibration_key("hybrid", rerank_tag(lambda q, s: [], "artifact"))
'hybrid+rerank-~anonymous+artifact'
```

### Module Attributes

| [`RERANK_TEXTS`](_autosummary/ir.rerank.html.md#ir.rerank.RERANK_TEXTS)          | The built-in `rerank_text` choices (a callable is also accepted).      |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`DFLT_RERANK_MODEL`](_autosummary/ir.rerank.html.md#ir.rerank.DFLT_RERANK_MODEL)     | The cross-encoder `rerank="cross-encoder"` resolves to (ef's default). |
| [`DFLT_RERANK_MAX_CHARS`](_autosummary/ir.rerank.html.md#ir.rerank.DFLT_RERANK_MAX_CHARS) | Cap on the characters of one `rerank_text="artifact"` passage.         |
| [`CROSS_ENCODER`](_autosummary/ir.rerank.html.md#ir.rerank.CROSS_ENCODER)         | The `rerank=` string that names ef's cross-encoder.                    |

### Functions

| [`resolve_reranker`](_autosummary/ir.rerank.html.md#ir.rerank.resolve_reranker)(spec)                         | The reranker `spec` names, or `None` when there is none to apply.                                                                                         |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`rerank_tag`](_autosummary/ir.rerank.html.md#ir.rerank.rerank_tag)(reranker[, rerank_text, max_chars]) | A short, key-safe identity for one reranked configuration (`None` if no rerank).                                                                          |
| [`is_anonymous`](_autosummary/ir.rerank.html.md#ir.rerank.is_anonymous)(tag)                              | Does `tag` rest on an unnamed callable (so its calibration key may collide)?                                                                              |
| [`spec_tag`](_autosummary/ir.rerank.html.md#ir.rerank.spec_tag)(spec[, rerank_text, max_chars])       | The tag a `rerank` spec *would* get, without loading a model; `None` if the spec cannot run here (a `"cross-encoder"` spec whose extra is not installed). |
| [`calibration_key`](_autosummary/ir.rerank.html.md#ir.rerank.calibration_key)(mode[, tag])                   | The key an abstention floor is stored and loaded under.                                                                                                   |
| [`passage_texts`](_autosummary/ir.rerank.html.md#ir.rerank.passage_texts)(corpus, candidates[, ...])       | The text the reranker scores for each candidate's store `meta` row.                                                                                       |

### ir.rerank.CROSS_ENCODER *= 'cross-encoder'*

The `rerank=` string that names ef’s cross-encoder.

### ir.rerank.DFLT_RERANK_MAX_CHARS *= 2000*

Cap on the characters of one `rerank_text="artifact"` passage. Cross-encoders truncate
at ~512 tokens anyway; the cap keeps the pair list cheap to build and the cut at a
surface boundary-agnostic, front-loaded point (name + description come first).

### ir.rerank.DFLT_RERANK_MODEL *= 'cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2'*

The cross-encoder `rerank="cross-encoder"` resolves to (ef’s default).

### ir.rerank.RERANK_TEXTS *= ('surface', 'artifact')*

The built-in `rerank_text` choices (a callable is also accepted).

### ir.rerank.calibration_key(mode, tag=None)

The key an abstention floor is stored and loaded under.

`mode` alone for a first-stage ranking (today’s behaviour, so existing floors keep
working); `"<mode>+<tag>"` for a reranked one.

```pycon
>>> calibration_key("hybrid")
'hybrid'
>>> calibration_key("hybrid", "rerank-m+artifact")
'hybrid+rerank-m+artifact'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### ir.rerank.is_anonymous(tag)

Does `tag` rest on an unnamed callable (so its calibration key may collide)?

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### ir.rerank.passage_texts(corpus, candidates, rerank_text='surface', , max_chars=2000)

The text the reranker scores for each candidate’s store `meta` row.

`"surface"` is the matched surface’s own text. `"artifact"` stitches every stored
surface of the candidate’s artifact in plan order (chunk overlap deduped, as in
[`ir.expand`](_autosummary/ir.html.md#ir.expand)) (siblings looked up once per
artifact, through the ledger) and cuts at `max_chars`; an artifact the ledger does not
know falls back to its matched surface. A callable is called as `rerank_text(corpus,
meta)`.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### ir.rerank.rerank_tag(reranker, rerank_text='surface', , max_chars=2000)

A short, key-safe identity for one reranked configuration (`None` if no rerank).

Built from the reranker’s identity (see `_identity()`), the `rerank_text` choice
and, for `"artifact"`, a non-default `max_chars` – everything that changes the
score scale. An unnamed reranker or text callable puts `~anonymous` in its tag, which
ir refuses to persist a floor under ([`is_anonymous()`](_autosummary/ir.rerank.html.md#ir.rerank.is_anonymous)). A tag longer than
`MAX_TAG_CHARS` is shortened with a hash of the whole, so it stays a usable file name.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### ir.rerank.resolve_reranker(spec)

The reranker `spec` names, or `None` when there is none to apply.

`spec` is `None` (no rerank), any `ef.Reranker` callable (returned as is), or the
string `"cross-encoder"` / `"cross-encoder:<model>"` – ef’s sentence-transformers
cross-encoder, built lazily and cached per model name (loading one is the expensive
part). If its optional dependency is absent this warns once and returns `None`, so
the caller degrades to first-stage ranking; resolve *before* deriving a calibration key
so the degraded run uses the plain key.

```pycon
>>> resolve_reranker(len) is len
True
>>> resolve_reranker("nope")
Traceback (most recent call last):
    ...
ValueError: unknown rerank spec 'nope'; expected a callable, 'cross-encoder' or 'cross-encoder:<model>'.
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### ir.rerank.spec_tag(spec, rerank_text='surface', , max_chars=2000)

The tag a `rerank` spec *would* get, without loading a model; `None` if the
spec cannot run here (a `"cross-encoder"` spec whose extra is not installed).

For lookups such as [`ir.eval.load_calibration()`](_autosummary/ir.eval.html.md#ir.eval.load_calibration), which need the key, not the model.


# _autosummary/ir.retrieve.html.md

# ir.retrieve

Retrieval — hard metadata filtering + dense / lexical / hybrid ranking.

[`search()`](_autosummary/ir.retrieve.html.md#ir.retrieve.search) embeds the query, applies a hard metadata filter to narrow the
candidate set (the `vd` Mongo-style filter language — ownership, name, tags),
then ranks the survivors. Three ranking modes share that one filtered candidate
set:

- `"dense"` (default) — exact brute-force cosine over the embedding matrix.
- `"lexical"` — Okapi BM25 over the candidates’ text (`vd.bm25_lexical_search`).
- `"hybrid"` — dense and lexical fused, either by Reciprocal Rank Fusion
  (`fusion="rrf"`, the default `vd.reciprocal_rank_fusion` rank-based fuse
  that sidesteps the cosine/BM25 score-scale mismatch) or by a
  magnitude-preserving convex blend (`fusion="blend"`) that keeps the dense
  cosine’s absolute scale for better abstention separability (see ir_08).

Hybrid matters for short, identifier-heavy capability text (skill / package /
tool names), the regime where dense-only retrieval fails silently on exact
identifiers and rare terms. An optional `rerank` hook (any
`ef.Reranker`) re-scores the top fused candidates with a cross-encoder;
it defaults to `None` so retrieval stays offline and API-free out of the box.

All ranking is exact brute force — correct and instant at `ir`’s corpus
sizes — and surface-hits collapse to the best surface per artifact. Lexical and
fusion reuse `vd`; if `vd` is unavailable, hybrid degrades to dense and
lexical returns no results (both with a warning), so a missing optional dep
never hard-fails a search.

Beyond the within-corpus channel fusion above, [`fuse_hits()`](_autosummary/ir.retrieve.html.md#ir.retrieve.fuse_hits) merges ranked
hit lists from **different sources** (corpora / embedders / modes) by weighted
Reciprocal Rank Fusion — raw scores never cross a source boundary, only ranks
do. It is the shared cross-source merge primitive consumed by federated
[`ir.discover()`](_autosummary/ir.html.md#ir.discover) and by an orchestration layer’s fan-in reranker (ir_09 §3).
Every search hit carries its corpus name as `source`
and its surface’s plan position as `surface_index`.

Two optional ranking signals act inside [`search()`](_autosummary/ir.retrieve.html.md#ir.retrieve.search): `surface_weights`
multiplies the first-stage score per surface kind, and `dep_boost` adds a
structural score per candidate after the reranker (the shipped
[`dependency_evidence_boost()`](_autosummary/ir.retrieve.html.md#ir.retrieve.dependency_evidence_boost) rewards dependencies on a caller-supplied
library set). Both default to off.

[`records_for_artifact()`](_autosummary/ir.retrieve.html.md#ir.retrieve.records_for_artifact) is the hit-operation beneath retrieval-time
context expansion: given a hit’s `artifact_id`, it returns *all* of that
artifact’s stored records (its sibling surfaces), ordered — resolved through
the ledger, never by re-deriving record ids. The expansion operator itself
(`ir.expand.expand()` — retrieve → expand → rerank) builds on it.

### Module Attributes

| [`MODES`](_autosummary/ir.retrieve.html.md#ir.retrieve.MODES)            | Ranking modes accepted by [`search()`](_autosummary/ir.retrieve.html.md#ir.retrieve.search).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`FUSIONS`](_autosummary/ir.retrieve.html.md#ir.retrieve.FUSIONS)          | Hybrid fusion methods accepted by [`search()`](_autosummary/ir.retrieve.html.md#ir.retrieve.search) (`mode="hybrid"`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| [`DFLT_RRF_K`](_autosummary/ir.retrieve.html.md#ir.retrieve.DFLT_RRF_K)       | RRF rank constant — the `k` of `1 / (k + rank)` (standard default 60).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| [`DFLT_BLEND_ALPHA`](_autosummary/ir.retrieve.html.md#ir.retrieve.DFLT_BLEND_ALPHA) | Dense weight in the `"blend"` fusion convex combination (`1-alpha` on the bounded lexical term).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| [`DFLT_BM25_SAT_K`](_autosummary/ir.retrieve.html.md#ir.retrieve.DFLT_BM25_SAT_K)  | `bm25 -> bm25/(bm25+k)`, a bounded squash to `[0, 1)` that needs no *per-query* normalization (which would erase the absolute-magnitude signal abstention calibration depends on).                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

### *exception* ir.retrieve.NoLedgerEntry

Bases: [`KeyError`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#KeyError)

The corpus has no ledger entry for the requested artifact.

The *benign* miss (unknown artifact, or a corpus built without ledger
bookkeeping) — distinct from a stale/torn ledger, which raises a plain
`KeyError` describing the corruption. A `KeyError` subclass so
existing `except KeyError` callers keep working; the disclosure seam
catches this one specifically and tolerates it per hit.

### ir.retrieve.as_retriever(corpus_or_name, \*\*search_defaults)

Bind ONE corpus to the uniform [`Retriever`](_autosummary/ir.retrieve.html.md#ir.retrieve.Retriever) contract.

Returns `retrieve(query, **overrides) -> list[SearchHit]` that calls
[`search()`](_autosummary/ir.retrieve.html.md#ir.retrieve.search) with `search_defaults` (a per-call kwarg overrides a bound
default). A corpus *name* is resolved once via [`ir.open_corpus()`](_autosummary/ir.html.md#ir.open_corpus); pass
an open [`Corpus`](_autosummary/ir.index.html.md#ir.index.Corpus) to skip that. The returned callable carries
the bound corpus on `.corpus` for introspection.

```pycon
>>> retr = as_retriever(corpus, mode="hybrid", k=20)
>>> hits = retr("how do I deploy the app")
>>> hits = retr("deploy", filter={"owner": "me"})
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`SearchHit`](_autosummary/ir.base.html.md#ir.base.SearchHit)]]

### ir.retrieve.dependency_evidence_boost(relevant_libs, , weight, saturate=1, deps_field='deps')

A `dep_boost` for [`search()`](_autosummary/ir.retrieve.html.md#ir.retrieve.search): reward dependencies on *relevant_libs*.

Reads the candidate’s `deps` filter field (as [`Package`](_autosummary/ir.strategy.html.md#ir.strategy.Package)
stores it), reduces each spec to its bare, PEP 503-normalized name, and
returns `weight * min(n, saturate) / saturate` where `n` counts the
dependencies found in *relevant_libs*. With the default `saturate=1` a
single relevant dependency earns the full `weight`. A structural signal,
cheap and model-free, that a prose reranker cannot be fooled out of: an
async-task package whose README says “DAG” does not depend on graph
libraries.

*relevant_libs* is the **caller’s** call: which libraries matter for a goal is
a planning decision that belongs to the agent layer, never to `ir`.
`weight` is added to the score on the search’s scale (an RRF fused score is
near `0.03`, a cosine near `0.5`, a sigmoid reranker in `(0, 1)`), so
tune it per configuration.

```pycon
>>> from ir.base import SearchHit
>>> boost = dependency_evidence_boost({"networkx"}, weight=0.1)
>>> boost(SearchHit("unbox", "description", 0.4, "", {"deps": ["networkx>=3"]}))
0.1
>>> boost(SearchHit("au", "description", 0.5, "", {"deps": ["anyio"]}))
0.0
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`SearchHit`](_autosummary/ir.base.html.md#ir.base.SearchHit)], [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]

### ir.retrieve.fuse_hits(hits_by_source, , rrf_k=60, weights=None, identity=None, k=None)

Merge per-source ranked hit lists into one ranking — by rank, not score.

The cross-source counterpart of the within-corpus hybrid fusion: scores
from different (corpus, mode, embedder) tuples live on incommensurable
scales (ir_07: “a different model re-scales everything”), so \*\*raw scores
never cross the source boundary\*\* — within each source they order and
dedup that source’s hits (one scale, sound), and across sources only ranks
interact, via weighted Reciprocal Rank Fusion: each hit contributes
`weights[source] / (rrf_k + rank)`.

* **Parameters:**
  * **hits_by_source** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None), [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`SearchHit`](_autosummary/ir.base.html.md#ir.base.SearchHit)]]) – `{source_name: ranked hits}`. Hits without a
    `source` are stamped with their mapping key (existing tags win,
    so one corpus bound under two keys still counts as one source).
    A `None` key is the *untagged pseudo-source*: its hits fuse as
    one rank group and stay unattributed (`source=None`). Within
    each list, duplicate artifacts — and, when `identity` is given,
    identity-duplicates — collapse to their best raw score before
    ranking, so a multi-query / multi-round pool can never
    double-count one artifact’s RRF mass.
  * **rrf_k** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – the RRF rank constant (standard default 60).
  * **weights** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – optional per-source trust dial (default 1.0 each) — a
    source’s contribution scales linearly, no score comparability
    needed. Keys naming sources absent from `hits_by_source` are
    ignored (a per-round pool may legitimately lack a configured
    source); callers with a closed source set should validate keys
    upfront, as federated [`ir.discover()`](_autosummary/ir.html.md#ir.discover) does.
  * **identity** ([`Union`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Union)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`SearchHit`](_autosummary/ir.base.html.md#ir.base.SearchHit)], [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]) – how cross-source duplicates merge — see [`Identity`](_autosummary/ir.retrieve.html.md#ir.retrieve.Identity).
    Default `None`: never; each `(source, artifact_id)` stays a
    distinct result.
  * **k** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – truncate the fused ranking to this many hits.
* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`SearchHit`](_autosummary/ir.base.html.md#ir.base.SearchHit)]
* **Returns:**
  the fused hits, best-first. Each carries the fused score in `score`
  and keeps its pre-fusion magnitude as `metadata["source_score"]` (+
  `"source_rank"`), so downstream consumers (abstention gates, LLM
  judges) never lose the per-source signal. When an `identity` merge
  combined several sources’ hits, `metadata["fused_sources"]` lists
  them and the representative hit is the one with the best rank.
  **Single-source input passes through with raw scores** (RRF of one
  list is that list’s order — same convention as the hybrid fusion’s
  single-channel fallback), so the fused-score rescaling only happens
  when there is genuinely something to fuse. The post-fusion `score`
  is ordinal: valid for ordering and relative cuts, meaningless against
  absolute floors — apply calibrated `min_score` floors per source,
  *before* fusing (see ir_07/ir_08 and `ir.discover`’s federated form).

### ir.retrieve.records_for_artifact(store_or_corpus, artifact_id, , surface_kind=None)

All stored records of *artifact_id*, ordered by `surface_index`.

The sibling-addressing primitive beneath retrieval-time context expansion:
a [`SearchHit`](_autosummary/ir.base.html.md#ir.base.SearchHit) names its artifact (and, via
`surface_index`, which surface of it matched);
this returns every surface of that artifact, in plan order, so an expansion
policy can stitch neighbors / parents around the hit.

Resolution is **ledger-backed only**: the artifact’s ledger entry lists its
`record_ids`. Record ids are never re-derived from a per-kind index like
`metadata["chunk_index"]` — on multi-kind strategies that index differs
from the plan-global `surface_index` baked into the id (see
[`ir.base.Record.make_id()`](_autosummary/ir.base.html.md#ir.base.Record.make_id)), so derivation would fetch wrong or missing
siblings.

* **Parameters:**
  * **store_or_corpus** – a [`CorpusStore`](_autosummary/ir.store.html.md#ir.store.CorpusStore), anything carrying
    one as `.store` (e.g. a [`Corpus`](_autosummary/ir.index.html.md#ir.index.Corpus)), or a corpus
    *name* — resolved straight to its local store: sibling lookup
    never embeds, so unlike [`ir.open_corpus()`](_autosummary/ir.html.md#ir.open_corpus) no embedder is
    loaded.
  * **artifact_id** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – the artifact whose surfaces to fetch.
  * **surface_kind** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – restrict to one surface kind (e.g. `"readme_chunk"`);
    a known artifact with no surfaces of that kind yields `[]`.
* **Raises:**
  * [**NoLedgerEntry**](_autosummary/ir.retrieve.html.md#ir.retrieve.NoLedgerEntry) – the ledger has no entry for *artifact_id* (an unknown
        artifact, or a corpus built without [`ir.index.build()`](_autosummary/ir.index.html.md#ir.index.build)’s
        ledger bookkeeping). A `KeyError` subclass.
  * [**KeyError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#KeyError) – an entry exists but lists a record missing from the store
        (a stale ledger: interrupted build or out-of-band
        `delete_record`) — data corruption, named in the message.
* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Record`](_autosummary/ir.base.html.md#ir.base.Record)]

### ir.retrieve.search(corpus, query, , k=10, filter=None, surfaces=None, per_artifact=True, mode='dense', fusion='rrf', rrf_k=60, alpha=0.5, bm25_sat_k=8.0, fetch_k=None, rerank=None, rerank_text='surface', rerank_max_chars=2000, bm25=None, formulate=None, surface_weights=None, dep_boost=None)

Return the top-*k* [`SearchHit`](_autosummary/ir.base.html.md#ir.base.SearchHit) for *query*.

* **Parameters:**
  * **k** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int))
  * **filter** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None))
  * **surfaces** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None))
  * **per_artifact** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool))
  * **mode** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – (dense + BM25 fused). Hybrid is the strongest default for short,
    identifier-heavy text; `"dense"` is the historical behavior and is
    kept as the default for backward compatibility.
  * **fusion** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – rank-based Reciprocal Rank Fusion) or `"blend"` (magnitude-preserving
    convex blend; better abstention separability — see ir_08). Ignored for
    non-hybrid modes.
  * **rrf_k** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int))
  * **alpha** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float))
  * **bm25_sat_k** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float))
  * **fetch_k** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – (default `max(k*5, 50)` when collapsing per artifact or reranking, else `k`).
  * **rerank** ([`Union`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Union)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]) – that re-scores the ranked candidates after fusion – the precision stage.
    The reranker sees the full candidate list (up to `fetch_k` items) and may
    reorder it; reranked hits carry the *reranker’s* score, which is on its own
    scale (see [`ir.rerank`](_autosummary/ir.rerank.html.md#module-ir.rerank), and [`ir.rerank.calibration_key()`](_autosummary/ir.rerank.html.md#ir.rerank.calibration_key) for
    abstention floors). Pass `"cross-encoder"` (or `"cross-encoder:<model>"`)
    for ef’s sentence-transformers cross-encoder, imported lazily; when that
    extra (`ir[rerank]`) is missing the search warns once and keeps the
    first-stage ranking. Default `None` keeps retrieval offline (no model
    download / API call).
  * **rerank_text** ([`Union`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Union)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)]) – (default; the matched surface’s text), `"artifact"` (the artifact’s
    sibling surfaces joined in plan order, so a thin description is judged
    against its full README), or a callable `(corpus, meta) -> str`.
  * **rerank_max_chars** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int))
  * **bm25** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – (e.g. `{"k1": 1.5, "b": 0.75}`).
  * **formulate** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]]) – [str, …]\`\`) applied *before* retrieval — rewrite / expand / HyDE
    (ir_09 §3). Identity by default (embed the query verbatim). When it
    returns several queries, ir runs each and fuses the results (best surface
    per artifact). See [`ir.make_llm_formulator()`](_autosummary/ir.html.md#ir.make_llm_formulator).
  * **surface_weights** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `{"deps": 2.0}` to let a high-precision `deps` surface outrank prose
    chunks. Each surface-hit’s first-stage score (the fused score in hybrid
    mode) is multiplied by its kind’s weight (default 1.0). Each channel
    still retrieves its own top `fetch_k`; the weights reorder those
    candidates (in hybrid mode, the whole fused union) before the cut to
    `fetch_k`, the reranker and the per-artifact collapse. Setting them
    makes the search over-fetch like `rerank` does, and formulated
    sub-searches inherit them. Kinds the corpus lacks are ignored; weights
    must be finite and non-negative. Meant for the non-negative scores of
    hybrid fusion and BM25 (a negative dense cosine moves *down* when
    multiplied by a weight above 1). Weighted scores are on a different scale
    from unweighted ones, so a calibrated floor does not apply to them
    (`discover(min_score="auto")` warns and skips it). Default `None`
    weighs every surface equally, as before.
  * **dep_boost** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`SearchHit`](_autosummary/ir.base.html.md#ir.base.SearchHit)], [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]]) – added to each fetched candidate’s score after fusion and the reranker,
    before the per-artifact collapse – a structural signal next to the
    reranker’s textual one. [`dependency_evidence_boost()`](_autosummary/ir.retrieve.html.md#ir.retrieve.dependency_evidence_boost) builds one from
    a caller-supplied library set. It reorders the fetched candidates (raise
    `fetch_k` to show it more); boosted scores need their own abstention
    floor (`discover(min_score="auto")` warns and skips it). Like
    `rerank` and `surface_weights`, it makes the search
    over-fetch (`max(k*5, 50)`) even with `per_artifact=False`, so pin
    `fetch_k` when comparing runs with and without it. Default `None`:
    no boost.
* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`SearchHit`](_autosummary/ir.base.html.md#ir.base.SearchHit)]


# _autosummary/ir.schedule.html.md

# ir.schedule

Install and operate the OS job that runs `ir maintain` — `ir schedule` (issue #75).

`ir maintain` is idempotent and cron-shaped, but something has to *call* it.
This module manages that caller: it writes a **definition** (a launchd plist or a
crontab line), hands it to the OS, and exits.

**\`\`ir\`\` still does not run a scheduler.** The boundary from issue #58 — “ir holds
the declarative policy as data and exposes an idempotent `ir maintain`; it does
not run a scheduler” — is preserved exactly. There is no daemon here, no event
loop, no in-process timer, and no orchestration import: launchd/cron remain the
executor, and this module is the *installer* for the crontab snippet
[`ir.maintenance`](_autosummary/ir.maintenance.html.md#module-ir.maintenance) already prescribes in its docstring. Turning that snippet
into a command is packaging, not a change of architecture.

The command is idempotent and tells you how to operate what it finds:

```default
ir schedule                # ensure a schedule exists; report + menu if one does
ir schedule --status       # report only, never mutates
ir schedule --every 30m    # set/change the interval
ir schedule --restart      # reload the definition, re-pinning the interpreter
ir schedule --remove       # stop it and delete the definition
ir schedule --dry-run      # print what would be written
```

**An existing definition is data, not a template to re-derive.** Only a *fresh*
install snapshots the calling shell’s environment. Every operation on a schedule
that already exists (`--every`, `--restart`) carries the stored environment
forward untouched, because the alternative silently re-points a working job at a
different corpus store the first time you operate it from a shell that happens to
lack `$PP` — which is the exact failure this module exists to prevent. Only
`--restart` re-pins the interpreter, and only because repairing a dead
interpreter is what it is for.

Two seams, both one keyword argument:

- `backend` — which OS scheduler holds the definition. Feature-detected
  (`launchctl` then `crontab`), never hardcoded per-platform; `systemd
  --user` timers are the documented next backend. A backend owns its own
  definition format, its own preview, and whether “loaded” means anything for it,
  so adding one touches [`BACKENDS`](_autosummary/ir.schedule.html.md#ir.schedule.BACKENDS) and nothing else.
- [`ScheduleSpec.args`](_autosummary/ir.schedule.html.md#ir.schedule.ScheduleSpec.args) — the command the job runs, defaulting to
  `-m ir maintain --all` pinned to the installing interpreter. An orchestration
  layer’s own entry point (#58 / ADR #43) drops in here without touching backends.

Everything else — the plist keys, the crontab line syntax, interval parsing,
output formatting — is written directly, on purpose.

### ir.schedule.BACKENDS *= (<class 'ir.schedule._LaunchdBackend'>, <class 'ir.schedule._CronBackend'>)*

Backends in preference order. launchd first on macOS because a LaunchAgent
survives reboots and logs where the OS expects; cron is the POSIX fallback and
also works on macOS if asked for by name.

This tuple is the whole seam. A backend owns its definition format, its
`preview`, and its `reports_loaded` answer, so adding `systemd --user`
means adding a class here and nothing else — no branch in the renderer, the
previewer, or the CLI.

### ir.schedule.DFLT_EVERY_MINUTES *= 60*

How often the job fires, in minutes. Hourly rather than the docstring
example’s 15 minutes: a `source-change` rebuild is a near-no-op only *after*
it has walked the sources, and a large corpus (tens of thousands of records)
makes that walk worth an hour’s spacing. `--every` moves it either way.

### ir.schedule.DFLT_LABEL *= 'com.i2mint.ir.maintain'*

Reverse-DNS job identifier. Also the launchd `Label` and the token that marks
ir’s line in the user crontab, so both backends find their own work and never
touch anybody else’s.

### ir.schedule.INHERITED_ENV_VARS *= ('IR_CONFIG_DIR', 'IR_DATA_DIR', 'IR_CACHE_DIR', 'XDG_CONFIG_HOME', 'XDG_DATA_HOME', 'XDG_CACHE_HOME', 'PP', 'PTH_FILEPATH')*

Variables a job must inherit to see what the shell that installed it sees.
launchd starts jobs with a near-empty environment and cron with a minimal one,
so anything ir reads from the environment has to be carried into the
definition or the job maintains a *different* (or empty) set of corpora.

`IR_*`/`XDG_*` locate the stores ([`ir.config`](_autosummary/ir.config.html.md#module-ir.config)); `PP` and
`PTH_FILEPATH` are read by [`ir.sources`](_autosummary/ir.sources.html.md#module-ir.sources) itself to find the package
manifest and the projects root, and without them the `packages` and
`reports` corpora fail outright — which is precisely how a scheduled job
ends up “running fine” while two of three corpora go stale.

### ir.schedule.LOAD_BEARING_ENV_VARS *= ('PP', 'PTH_FILEPATH')*

Of those, the ones whose absence breaks a corpus outright rather than merely
relocating it. [`status()`](_autosummary/ir.schedule.html.md#ir.schedule.status) reports a job that lacks one the current shell
has, because that job is failing silently right now.

### *exception* ir.schedule.ScheduleError

Bases: [`Exception`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#Exception)

A schedule could not be read, written, or expressed on this platform.

### *class* ir.schedule.ScheduleSpec(every_minutes=60, python=<factory>, args=('-u', '-m', 'ir', 'maintain', '--all'), label='com.i2mint.ir.maintain', log_path=<factory>, env=\_job_env())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

What to run and how often — backend-independent.

`python` is pinned to an absolute interpreter path (by default the one
installing the schedule) because neither launchd nor cron inherits the shell’s
`PATH`-resolved `ir`. Pinning is also what makes staleness *detectable*:
[`status()`](_autosummary/ir.schedule.html.md#ir.schedule.status) can check the recorded interpreter still exists.

Python block-buffers stdout when it is not a tty, so
without it a scheduled run’s log stays empty until the process exits —
exactly when you most want to watch a slow rebuild.

* **Type:**
  `-u` matters
